title: Van Flandern alerts Harrington to Pioneer 10 data on a planet beyond the Kuiper belt
place_text: US Naval Observatory; outer solar system

tellings.quote: he calls up Robert Harton he's like hey Robert you gotta check out this data from Pioneer 10

plain: In the 1980s, the story goes, the astronomer Thomas Van Flandern of the US Naval Observatory phoned his colleague Robert Harrington and told him he had to look at data from Pioneer 10, a NASA space probe heading out of the solar system, because it hinted at an unknown planet beyond the Kuiper belt, the band of icy bodies past Neptune. The researcher Matt LaCroix tells Michels this, passing on what the two astronomers are said to have found. If true, a large unseen planet would be lurking at the edge of our solar system.
